chapter: Dancing schools, Sapiro and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Morton's planned band with Omer Simeon, Barney Bigard and Paul Barbarin
summary: Morton imported Omer Simeon and other players and rehearsed a band at the Renaissance meant for Roseland; Procope regrets it never got started.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Yeah. I just had the 78 at home. I've got it home. But you see, Jelly Roll, he had these big ideas which are very good, and during the time we were playing at the Rose Danceland, he imported Omer Simeon from New York and there's another clarinet player named Blue. Blue was from St. Louis. And --
You mean Omer Simeon he imported from New Orleans.
Well, he was in Chicago at the time.

He was originally from New Orleans, but he came up to Chicago. And he had Paul Barbarin. He was on his way to, you know, build up something, you know. Then the only thing -- there's one thing I always regretted. Then he started rehearsing the band up at the Renaissance, and
he was supposed to take this band in the Roseland, see. Rose Danceland and Roseland is two different places.

And this band he was rehearsing, he had Omer Sim?on, Barney Bigard and myself in the reed section. And who were the trumpets? He had a fellow named -- I can't remember, I can see him, but I can't remember the name. Paul Barbarin was on drums. Oh, I can't remember the names. But I always thought that if that had of gotten off the ground, you know, I would have liked that very much, because the people he had in the band were great jazz players, like Omer Simeon and Barney Bigard and I think he had Louis Metcalf on trumpet, and -- I can see the guy right now. I can't think of his name. (probably Ward Pinkett) Anyway --
But he wrote the arrangements himself.
And they were very -- were they more imaginative than most arrangements in that time?

Yeah. Yeah. If he had been able to get it to going and get this job and get to playing on this job, I believe he would have had one of the great bands. Because it was all there. It just didn't get off the ground.
